title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This act focuses on building a skilled workforce for the AI industry by investing in education, training, and research. It aims to boost innovation, create high‑tech jobs, and enhance the country’s competitiveness in the global AI market.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill aims to create a system for providing detailed, standardized lists of all parts and components used in artificial‑intelligence products, making it easier to understand and trace how AI systems are built. It also includes other related provisions to support the implementation and oversight of such materials.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act aims to give schools clear guidance on how to use artificial intelligence tools in teaching. It also sets standards for transparency, privacy, and training to ensure safe and effective use of AI in education.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed AI education into schools, creating a nationwide curriculum that teaches students the basics of AI and how to use it responsibly. It also establishes teacher training and funding programs to help educators support AI‑ready learning environments across the country.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes rules to keep AI-powered toys safe for kids, including strict standards for design, manufacturing, and testing. It also requires clear labeling, limits on data collection, and penalties for companies that fail to meet these safety and privacy requirements.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy states that every American and community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center deserves clear information about the project and the right to make decisions that reflect their own interests. It emphasizes transparency and local control as essential rights in the development and operation of AI data centers.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the creation or operation of AI data centers on lands owned or managed by the federal government. This law would ensure that federal property is not used for large-scale AI infrastructure, preserving those lands for other purposes.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is designed to ensure that artificial intelligence systems used in veterans' services are safe, ethical, and transparent. It establishes oversight mechanisms and standards to protect veterans' rights and wellbeing when AI is employed in healthcare, benefits, and decision‑making processes.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Act establishes rules to prevent AI from creating or spreading fake content that could be used to exploit individuals or groups. It sets out measures for verification, accountability, and enforcement to ensure AI systems cannot be employed for harmful fabricated exploitation.

title: A bill to require a report on the artificial intelligence power of the People's Republic of China.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: This bill requires the production of a comprehensive report evaluating China’s artificial intelligence capabilities, including research, industry, and infrastructure. The report aims to inform policy decisions and assess the country's position in the global AI landscape.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying how artificial intelligence affects judicial processes and creates oversight mechanisms to ensure the technology is used fairly and transparently. It aims to promote accountability, protect privacy, and maintain public trust in court decisions that involve AI.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires that a report be filed on how artificial intelligence is used to access and process unminimized information gathered under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It also includes provisions for additional matters related to AI usage.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 seeks to stop AI systems from colluding to fix prices or manipulate markets, protecting consumers and fostering fair competition. The law requires companies to disclose algorithmic strategies and imposes penalties on those that facilitate or participate in collusive behavior.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 aims to cut the United States’ reliance on Chinese AI technology and talent by limiting imports, investments, and collaborations that could benefit China’s AI industry. It seeks to boost domestic AI development, secure national security interests, and create incentives for U.S. companies to build and supply AI solutions independently of Chinese supply chains.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act seeks to broaden the range of perspectives and voices involved in creating and using artificial intelligence. It aims to promote diversity, inclusion, and equitable participation in AI decision‑making and deployment.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a legislative proposal aimed at regulating the development and use of artificial intelligence in the Homestake region. It is likely designed to ensure that AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with community values and local economic interests.

title: LEARN AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
summary: The LEARN AI Act proposes new rules for designing and using AI systems that learn from data, focusing on safety and ethical standards. It aims to make these systems more transparent, protect user privacy, and encourage responsible innovation.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act aims to protect children’s personal data from being collected, shared, or used by AI systems without clear safeguards. It requires companies to obtain parental consent, provide transparent data practices, and implement strong security measures to keep youth information private.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a law that will require schools to teach students about artificial intelligence, including how it works, how to use it responsibly, and how it affects society. It aims to give students the knowledge and skills they need to understand and safely engage with AI technology in their future careers and everyday lives.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 aims to boost AI learning across schools and universities. It proposes funding and resources to help educators teach and students learn AI skills.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at protecting U.S. artificial‑intelligence models from being copied or distributed without permission. It establishes penalties and enforcement measures to discourage theft and safeguard intellectual property rights.
